chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When you enshroud the deceased, scatter upon every cloth something from the fragrant powder and camphor.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended method for embalming the deceased in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes the application of tharidrah and camphor to the shrouds, reflecting the Shia emphasis on honoring the deceased with fragrance as a sign of respect and preparation for the Hereafter. This practice is rooted in the Prophetic tradition of embalming and serves to distinguish the burial rites of the faithful, linking physical preparation with spiritual dignity.
